Cohomology/TildeExactness.lean is now entirely sorry-free -- this was that file's long-open named target, with a header section literally titled "Why tildePreservesFiniteLimits itself is NOT closed here".

LANDED: tilde_preservesMonomorphisms, tildePreservesFiniteLimits, tilde_preservesHomology, plus the supporting sectMap / sectMap_eq / tilde_injective_app_basicOpen.

ROUTE -- basic opens, not stalks. Basic opens are a basis of Spec R, and mathlib ALREADY exhibits Gamma(M~, D(r)) as a localisation of M at the powers of r (tilde.toOpen carries an IsLocalizedModule.Away instance). So the section map of ~f over D(r) IS IsLocalizedModule.map of f (by IsLocalizedModule.ext against the naturality square tilde.toOpen_map_app), injective by IsLocalizedModule.map_injective since localisation is flat. Basis injectivity gives stalkwise injectivity hence mono; right exactness is free (left adjoint); right exact + mono-preserving => left exact.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING AS A LESSON, not just a result. The file's own header prescribed a DIFFERENT route and estimated 100-150 LOC for it: R-linearity of the Ab STALK map, then a jointly-reflecting stalk family through JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.jointlyReflectsLimit, with a long warning that the ModuleCat-valued stalk path is dead because mathlib keeps toStalk_l / stalkIso_l / stalkToLocalization_l private. NONE of that is needed on the basic-open route: the injectivity check happens BEFORE any stalk is formed, so no stalk colimit and no jointly-reflecting step enters, and the R-linearity that matters is on SECTIONS where Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul supplies it in one line. A carefully-written plan in a docstring is evidence about ONE route, not about the difficulty of the statement. The header has been corrected in place; the section-1 stalk material is retained as the sharpest per-point statement.
